status.currentFacts: The shared runtime registry and base geometry exist in src/core/ui-system.*. Button is adopted by shared toolbar/actions and parts of the browser; card and field are adopted by the shared AIC renderer; toolbar, menu, notice, and tree are partially adopted in the browser. Most legacy selectors remain active and required.
status.approvedDirection: The user approved one cross-host design system using BEM elements and explicit modifiers for Standard Notes, Chromium, and VS Code. The eight current IDs are the implemented technical baseline accepted in root review, not names separately prescribed by the user.
status.reviewPending: The mappings below are the author's recommended migration map. Reviewers must approve or amend each mapping before removing legacy hooks.

naming.policy: New shared visual identity uses BEM classes. Host-specific classes may remain for integration layout or native platform hooks, but must not redefine the component contract.

components.purpose: Named native action control with consistent geometry, focus, disabled state, variant, size, and optional custom SVG mask icon with a separate text label. Primary actions use the semantic accent and on-accent tokens. Icon-only copy feedback keeps the accessible action name stable, announces status, briefly shows a success checkmark or failure cross, and restores its original icon. Unsaved changes accent and softly pulse only the save button, with a static reduced-motion cue.

A compact wrapping group of context title and actions that avoids horizontal scrolling and retains 44 px coarse-pointer targets; behavior, optional local-guide placement, and save ownership remain with the host. The PWA places optional supported local AI in the existing compact editor toolbar and moves save status/retry to its note header.

Bounded contextual choice surface with compact left-aligned action rows, decorative SVG icons, subtle section titles, separators, hints, focus entry, dismissal, and host-owned action callbacks. PWA document, workspace, Open and Help sheets use shared native actions with host-owned placement, focus restoration and lifecycle cleanup.

Non-secret status, success, warning, progress, or actionable error feedback with optional actions and accessible live-region semantics. Browser recovery notices show only the number of available draft copies and an explicit review action; draft contents stay out of feedback.

Labelled value/control unit with validation, masking, independently typed parts, help, error, and accessible action relationships. Composite AIC rows give labels and typed values natural width, wrap whole items before breaking long text, use compact lock-only password copy targets, and attach creation controls to the final part. Short card/TOTP values stay intact; unlabelled rows omit the label and coarse-pointer controls retain 44 px targets. Icon-only copy targets show temporary success checkmarks with accessible status; subtle gray row alternation supports scanning.

Structured content surface with header, title, body, and actions for AIC fields, diagrams, errors, and compact read-only previews. AIC sections use larger headings and distinct neutral group backgrounds to separate their rows visually. Details keep wrapping summary titles and source actions separate, with inset child previews and one visible parent boundary. Code bodies scroll only horizontally and allow vertical gestures to continue scrolling the document.

Hierarchical or ordered navigation metadata with groups, items, rows, labels, and actions; it never owns note content. Connected navigation uses native nested lists and disclosure groups, with compact SVG folder/document icons, ownership guide lines, single-line labels and touch-aware rows. Browser and PWA share the same geometry.

Expose the current editing identity and its non-owning shared, ancestor, source, or path context without merging content or persistence identities. Mutually exclusive accessible scope tabs keep one panel visible and focusable, support manual keyboard activation and defer transitions to the host save barrier. The document variant shares a compact source-location and acknowledged-save-status strip across PWA, browser and VS Code without owning persistence. Scope tabs use inset selected surfaces with a full subtle border, without an underline; keyboard focus is inset and touch targets remain 44px.

coverageGaps: The eight IDs describe reusable primitives, not every composed feature widget. Diagram builder, table cell editor, Mermaid viewport, and CodeMirror editor remain composed patterns over these primitives plus integration-specific hooks.
Legacy selectors are grouped by ownership and migration target, not enumerated as a frozen compatibility API. A selector audit must precede each removal.

VS Code native workbench views, editor associations, and commands cannot be restyled by webview CSS; only AIC-owned webview controls can adopt these classes. The former extension-specific TreeDataProvider is retired.
Current adoption is additive. No claim is made that all hosts or all legacy selectors have been converted.
